result.title: MARC: Mechanism-Aware Reflective Correction for Articulated Object Code Generation
result.summary: Generating an articulated object from images and text requires more than plausible parts and movable joints: the assembled mechanism must execute the intended motion. This is particularly challenging for closed-chain and coupled mechanisms, where an error in one connection can block motion or separate connected parts. We introduce MARC, Mechanism-Aware Reflective Correction, which shares an executable kinematic graph across program construction, motion solving, and correction. The graph binds physical connections to local attachment frames and represents loop closures and joint-coordinate couplings. Given prescribed driver inputs, a numerical solver computes follower motion and associates errors with specific connections and configurations. The agent uses these diagnostics to probe possible causes, revise connections or geometry, and retest the mechanism along the original motion paths. On a 20-object test set, MARC with Kimi-K3 achieves 67.8% valid motion coverage and 60.0% overall success, outperforming six baselines. Starting from the same initial candidates, correction improves these scores by 13.7 and 20.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablations further show the benefits of graph-based mechanism support and graph-guided repair. Project homepage: https://demianmusk.github.io/MARC-Home/.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MARC，用一张共享的可执行运动学图串联图像/文本到关节物体的代码构造、运动求解与纠错；数值求解器把误差归因到具体连接与配置，agent 据此探查原因、修改几何或连接并沿原运动路径重测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「结构化诊断→定位到具体组件与配置→针对性修正并重测」的闭环，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据获取、修正与停止决策提供可核查的方法线索；但任务本身是 3D 关节物体代码生成，与 latent 推理状态的直接联系需进一步判断。
